newsitem.title: MOROCCO: BOXING-RAHILOU MOUNTS FIRST DEFENCE OF WBA WORLD TITLE.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-RAHILOU MOUNTS FIRST DEFENCE OF WBA WORLD TITLE.

text.p: Khalid Rahilou mounts the first defence of his World Boxing Association (WBA) junior welterweight title on Saturday against American Marty Jakubowski.
The French-born Rahilou is also a Moroccan citizen and can expect solid support from the home crowd in Casablanca.
"I'm in good shape after two months' intensive training in Paris," Rahilou, 31, told journalists after arriving in Casablanca. "And I am determined to win, especially here in Morocco."
The boxer, 1.71 metres tall, has been beaten twice and won 28 bouts, 15 of them inside the distance.
He took the WBA title last January against American Frankie Randall in Nashville, Tennessee, 58 seconds into the 11th round when the referee stopped the fight.
But his opponent Jakubowski, three years his junior and standing 1.74 metres, has an impressive record of 98 victories, including 25 knockouts, and three defeats.
Rahilou began his international career as an amateur and represented Morocco at the 1988 Seoul Olympics where he lost to American Todd Foster after five minutes and a knockdown.
He began as a professional in France in 1991 and twice became European light-welterweight champion, in 1994 and 1995.
Jakubowski is ranked eighth by the WBA and has been professional since the age of 17.
His coach Wesley Ramey said. "I watched Rahilou in Tennessee. Randall had no legs because of Khalid's speed and technique. But Marty has really good legs and can box and punch.
"I think a lot of people will be surprised by all the things Marty can do. I have a big suitcase in my room to bring the (WBA) belt back to Indiana," he said.
Rahilou's French manager Michel Acaries said: "Rahilou is in pretty good shape. The important thing is for him to keep his concentration for the last days before the fight.
"It will be a very tough fight. Jakubowski's entourage is very serious. They are here to take the title. We are here to keep it."
